transcript: Meeting header: 2027-02-14 16:00 UTC | Duration: ~60 minutes | Attendees: Sasha (Redwood AE), Jordan (CSM), Ethan (SE)  Maya, Tom, Aisha (Lakeview)
[00:00] Sasha: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, happy Valentine's week, appreciate you making time. quick round of intros then we'll go into what the success criteria looks like for Lakeview 

[00:18] Maya: Hey, I'm Maya, I run Data & ML. We're focused on using LLMs for clinical note summarization and some triage workflows. Main concerns are PHI handling, latency to clinicians, and integration into our EHR inbox.

[00:36] Tom: Tom here, IT. I'm responsible for network, firewall, and onboarding private endpoints. we need to understand VPC peering and egress policies. also curious about logging/retention for audits.
[00:50] Aisha: Aisha, compliance. SOC2 is in place, and we require KMS integration with our cloud HSM for keys, audit trails, and SSO. we'll want to see the data retention and delete flows.

[01:05] Jordan: Awesome, thanks. Quickly from our side, goal of today is to align on deployment choice  looks like you're leaning private/VPC  go over pilot scope and assign next steps. Ethan will cover the technical bits after a short timeline proposal.

[01:22] Ethan: Hi all. High level, Redwood supports Hosted, Dedicated, and Private. For PHI and your compliance needs, Private (VPC peering + customer KMS) is usually the right fit. There are some tradeoffs on latency and ops surface but we can walk through the baseline architecture.

[01:40] Maya: Yes, private is preferable. performance is important though  clinicians need sub-second to low single-second for summaries ideally. what are realistic latencies for the timeline and model choices?

[01:55] Ethan: For the typical summarization models, on Dedicated or Private with reserved GPUs and optimized kernels we often see 400-800ms for 256 token outputs, depends on model variant, batching, and KV cache. We can run benchmarks during pilot to match your SLA. Note: if you need extreme low latency we can recommend a smaller, quantized model or Dedicated capacity.
[02:18] Tom: OK, can you elaborate on the network setup? Peering, NAT, egress? We have strict egress rules and will need to open minimal ports.

[02:28] Ethan: Sure. For Redwood Private we do VPC peering or PrivateLink depending on cloud. The minimal egress is to Redwood control plane for metrics and management  if you want fully air-gapped there's an on-prem option but that requires more ops. We'll send a network diagram. sometimes the nomenclature in our docs shows 'Redwood control plane' and it gets mixed with 'control plan' in auto transcripts  sorry.

[02:48] Aisha: On KMS  we need server-side encryption with our KMS, HSM-backed keys, and a key rotation policy. Also, audit logs need to be retained for 7 years for certain contracts. Do you have SOC2 docs and audit logging capabilities?

[03:05] Jordan: We do have SOC2 Type II report and can share it. We also support customer-managed KMS. For audit logs, Redwood Console provides per-request logs and exports; default retention varies but enterprise packages include long-term retention. We'll share the security pack.

[03:25] Maya: Great. For pilot success criteria: accuracy on summarization (ROUGE/ human eval), latency under 1s for clinician flows, and integration into EHR with acceptable throughput of X req/min. We'll send exact numbers.
[03:40] Sasha: That sounds good. Jordan  timeline? I think a two-week discovery and environment prep, then 4-week pilot. Thoughts?

[03:49] Jordan: That aligns. Suggested plan: week 0 discovery (this week)  collect network diagram, SSO metadata, KMS info. Week 1 environment readiness and sandbox setup. Weeks 2-5 pilot runs and benchmarks with sample prompts. Final review week 6. We can compress but prefer this cadence.
[04:10] Tom: For sandbox we need an IP allowlist and a staging VPC peering. I'll need the exact CIDRs and endpoints. Also would like the port list.

[04:20] Ethan: We'll provide an infra readiness checklist, endpoints, and a sample CloudFormation / Terraform snippet for setting up peering. Note: depending on your cloud provider some things differ (AWS PrivateLink vs GCP VPC peering). We'll ask for your provider and region.
[04:40] Maya: We're on AWS us-east-1. We'll share specific VPC CIDR and security team contact after the call.
[04:49] Aisha: A couple of typical compliance questions: do you do data-in-transit encryption? can we configure log export to our SIEM? how do you handle deletion requests?

[05:00] Jordan: Yes, TLS in transit, AES-256 at rest with customer KMS option. We support syslog/CloudWatch export to your SIEM. Deletion flows: we can purge request logs and model inputs per policy and document those processes. We'll include details in the security pack.

[05:20] Sasha: Also to highlight, for cost and performance optimization Redwood Optimize can run initial profiling and suggest batching/quantization settings if you'd like  helpful to meet latency and cost targets in pilot.
[05:33] Maya: That would be useful, yes. We have budget constraints and want to balance latency and inference costs. If you can recommend quantization profiles that keep accuracy high that's ideal.

[05:45] Ethan: We'll plan a short eval matrix: 1) baseline model, 2) quantized variant, 3) smaller low-latency variant  benchmark latency, tokens/sec, and a small human eval for quality. We'll feed results back in a shared spreadsheet.
[06:05] Tom: On SSO  we use Okta. We'll need SAML metadata and a service account. Jordan, do you have an SSO setup guide?
[06:15] Jordan: Yes, we have a step-by-step SSO/SAML guide and can do a quick setup session with your identity team. We'll include the required attributes and sample metadata file.
[06:30] Aisha: One more thing: data residency. Some of our records are stored in EU and we need to ensure certain datasets don't leave region. Is region pinning possible?

[06:40] Ethan: Yes  you can pin deployments to a region. For Redwood Private we provision inferencing capacity in your region or on your VPC. We'll capture the exact data flow to ensure no cross-region egress for those datasets. We'll need to review the sample data flows.

[06:58] Sasha: Great. Let's capture owners and due dates quickly. Jordan  share playbook and security pack by Thursday. Tom  provide network diagram by Monday. Maya  send prompt sets and success criteria by Friday. Ethan  prepare VPC/KMS deep dive doc and propose slots for the follow-up call. We'll send calendar invites.
[07:20] Maya: Sounds good. Quick question on backups and KV cache  how are model context caches handled? There was some confusion in our infra team last week.

[07:30] Ethan: Right  Redwood uses KV caching to accelerate repeated prefixes; that cache is ephemeral; for PHI you likely want to avoid persistent prefix caches unless you control encryption keys. We'll document our default behavior and options for disabling caches. Sometimes transcripts show KV as \u2018K-V cache\u2019 or \u2018K V cache\u2019 \u0014 apologies for the stutter in auto transcripts.
[07:55] Tom: Thanks. Any blockers from your side for starting the sandbox?
[08:00] Jordan: Not from us. We'll just need the items we listed. Sasha, anything else to close with?

[08:08] Sasha: No, just excited to get started. I'll follow up with proposed times for the technical deep dive and the SE will prepare the infra docs. We'll also open a shared Drive folder with the playbook and benchmark sheet. Thanks everyone.
[08:20] Maya: Thanks all, appreciate it. Bye.
[08:24] End of recording.
